chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Prayer is not performed over the newborn who has not yet cried out, nor is he validly inherited, nor is blood money (diyah) paid for him from either ransom or other sources. But if he cries out, then pray over him and inherit him.

Thus, this report is to be understood as indicating a type of preferability (istihbab) or precautionary piety (taqiyyah), so that it does not contradict what we have previously established, and it adds clarification to what we have mentioned.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Precautionary piety or dissimulation to avoid harm or contradiction
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: Blood money or compensation paid for killing
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: Preferability or recommended status in jurisprudence
key_terms.الْمَنْفُوسِ: The newborn infant, specifically one who has not yet cried out
key_terms.يَسْتَهِلَّ: To cry out or make a sound, indicating life and viability

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for performing funeral prayer and inheritance over a newborn infant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for infant funeral prayer and inheritance, linking the physical act of 'crying out' (istihlal) to legal personhood. The scholar notes that the exclusion of the pre-cry infant from these rites is likely due to *istihbab* (preferability) or *taqiyyah* (precautionary piety) to avoid contradicting established principles, highlighting the nuanced interplay between biological signs and ritual law in Shia fiqh.
